# About Me

I'm a UCLA graduate student pursuing my MS in Biostatistics at the [Fielding School of Public Health](https://ph.ucla.edu/), with a research focus on Bayesian methods and their applications in neuroimaging. My work combines dynamic functional connectivity analysis from resting-state fMRI data with advanced statistical tools, including Gaussian graphical models and causal mediation analysis, to study the brain mechanisms underlying neurodegenerative diseases such as frontotemporal dementia (FTD).

I'm passionate about mathematical and statistical methods for Bayesian modeling and brain connectivity analysis to push the boundaries of computational neuroscience and brain-computer interfaces, and to contribute to the future of diagnosis and treatment in neurodegenerative diseases.
